scale_009:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up {{vendor}} (our incident management platform) as part of on-call & incident response setup. Goal: prepare a full set of services in {{vendor}}, one per key system/team we need to alert on, ready for my review and approval before anything is actually created.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) our {{vendor}} account/org details and confirmation you should use my configured credentials, (2) the list of systems or teams needing services (e.g. API backend, database, payments, frontend, infra) — ask me to confirm or supply this if not given, (3) which observability tools we use (Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, CloudWatch, Sentry, or others) so integrations can be matched, (4) any naming convention or escalation policy names I already use.

Then, using the {{vendor}} public API or dashboard, draft a proposed configuration for each service: name, description, the escalation policy it should attach to (use existing ones if named, otherwise flag as 'needs escalation policy'), and which monitoring integration(s) should route alerts into it based on documented first-party integration setup for that tool. Note any routing conditions I specify (e.g. severity-based routing).

Do not create or apply anything yet. Compile the full draft list of services with their attributes and integrations into a clear summary (table or structured list) and present it to me for review.

Once presented, stop for human sign-off — do not create, submit, or apply any service in {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve the draft. Report back with the complete draft list, any open questions (e.g. missing escalation policies, ambiguous team ownership), and a note confirming you are awaiting my approval before making changes.

scale_009:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up on-call rotation schedules in {{vendor}} (our incident-management tool) using its API with my configured credentials. Approval is required before any changes go live, so you must prepare everything but stop short of activating it.

First, ask me for: (1) the list of teams/services needing on-call coverage, (2) the engineers on each team and their time zones, (3) desired rotation pattern (e.g., weekly, daily, follow-the-sun) and rotation start day/time, (4) any layered coverage needs (e.g., primary/secondary), and (5) whether round-robin ordering should be applied.

Then do the following:
1. Draft a schedule configuration for each team: name, time zone, rotation layers, rotation length, and member order, using the documented public API for creating rotation schedules.
2. Confirm that each schedule will expose a calendar feed engineers can subscribe to, and prepare the feed setup as part of the draft.
3. Prepare the ability for engineers to self-serve overrides, shift swaps, and coverage requests without needing an admin to rebuild the schedule — document how this will work once live.
4. Compile a clear summary showing: schedules to be created, rotation logic, time zones, layering, and calendar feed access — formatted so I can review it easily.
5. Do NOT create, activate, or push any schedule changes live. Only prepare drafts, configs, and a review checklist.

When finished, report back with: the full draft configuration per team/schedule, the calendar feed setup plan, the self-service override/swap mechanism description, and a checklist of what will be created once approved. Then stop for human sign-off — do not submit, activate, or finalize any schedule until I explicitly approve it.

scale_009:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure escalation policies in {{vendor}} as part of setting up our on-call & incident response system. Escalation policies define how an unacknowledged page moves through responders (delays, fallback responders, repeat rounds) until someone acknowledges it.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our {{vendor}} account access (use your configured credentials), the list of on-call teams/services that need escalation policies, the responder order for each (individuals, schedules, or teams), acceptable delay/timeout intervals between escalation steps, how many rounds to repeat before declaring no-ack, and any fallback responders (e.g., a manager or secondary team) for final escalation. Also confirm which notification channels (push, SMS, phone call, email) each responder wants and any per-channel rules they've specified.

Using {{vendor}}'s documented public API or dashboard, draft the escalation policy configuration for each service/team: the ordered escalation steps, timeout durations, repeat count, and final fallback responder. Do not create or apply any live changes yet — prepare a clear, complete draft (one policy per team/service) showing exactly what will be created, including step order, delays, and notification channel assumptions.

Compile this into a checklist/summary document for my review, listing each proposed escalation policy, its steps, and any assumptions you made where I didn't provide explicit input. Flag any gaps (e.g., missing fallback responder) that need my decision.

Once the draft is ready, present it to me and stop for human sign-off — do not create, submit, or activate any escalation policy in {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve the configuration.

scale_009:n4.prompt:
You are helping me connect our error-tracking tool ({{vendor}}) to PagerDuty so application errors and alerts automatically create tracked incidents with proper routing and escalation. This requires human approval before going live, so prepare everything but do not activate or finalize the integration yourself.

First, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account/org details and the project(s) whose errors should trigger incidents, (2) which PagerDuty escalation policy and on-call schedule should receive these alerts, (3) severity thresholds or rules for what counts as an incident-worthy error (e.g., new issue, regression, error rate spike) versus what should just be logged, and (4) any silencing/grouping preferences to avoid noisy or duplicate alerts.

Then: draft the alerting rule configuration in {{vendor}} that defines which error events should notify via webhook, specify the webhook destination pointing to PagerDuty's alert intake, and map severity/urgency levels to the correct PagerDuty escalation policy. Document how issues will appear in PagerDuty (grouped by {{vendor}} issue, with stack trace/release links preserved for context) and how resolution/regression in {{vendor}} should reflect back as incident resolution in PagerDuty, if supported.

Use your configured credentials to access both platforms as needed for configuration and testing in a non-production or sandboxed way if possible. Do not enable the live webhook or apply the routing rule that will begin triggering pages.

When done, give me: a summary of the configured rule and routing logic, the specific escalation policy it targets, screenshots or exported config details, and a clear list of what will happen once activated. Then stop for human sign-off before enabling the connection.

scale_009:n5.prompt:
You are helping me complete one step of setting up incident response: creating the dedicated incident chat channel in our {{vendor}} team-chat workspace, as part of standing up PagerDuty-based on-call and incident workflows.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) confirmation of the {{vendor}} workspace/org my configured credentials point to, (2) the desired channel name (e.g. 'incidents' or 'incident-response'), and (3) whether it should be a public/open channel or restricted, and who should have membership (on-call responders, incident commanders, etc.).

Once I provide these, prepare (but do not execute without my sign-off) the following:
1. The exact command to create the channel using the {{vendor}} CLI, in the form: `{{vendor}} channels create --name "<channel-name>" --type stream --visibility open` (adjust visibility flag if I asked for restricted access).
2. A short description/topic for the channel explaining its purpose (e.g. 'Live incident coordination channel — used during active incidents, linked from PagerDuty alerts').
3. A checklist of follow-up configuration to consider: inviting the on-call/escalation group, connecting an incoming webhook so PagerDuty alerts can post into the channel, and optionally adding an AI agent bot that can be mentioned during incidents for automated help.
4. A note on how membership controls will be applied given my visibility choice.

Do not run the create command or invite anyone yet — present the fully drafted command, description, and checklist, then explicitly stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied.

Report back with: the exact command prepared, the proposed channel name/description, the visibility/membership plan, and the pending follow-up checklist, clearly flagged as awaiting my approval.

scale_009:n6.prompt:
You are helping me create a standardized post-mortem template for our incident response process, to be stored in {{vendor}} (our project-management tool). If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} workspace or team space where this should live, (2) any existing folder/database it should be filed under, (3) our company name and product name for template branding, and (4) any specific incident-severity or escalation terminology we use (e.g., SEV1/SEV2) so the template matches our PagerDuty setup.

Once you have these, draft a post-mortem template as a new page in {{vendor}} using its page-creation API (create a new page, analogous to POST /v1/pages), containing these sections:
- Title placeholder: 'Post-Mortem: [Incident Name] — [Date]'
- Summary (one-paragraph overview)
- Severity & Impact (customers affected, duration, revenue/SLA impact)
- Timeline (timestamped sequence of detection, escalation, mitigation, resolution — cross-reference PagerDuty incident ID field)
- Root Cause Analysis
- Contributing Factors
- What Went Well
- What Went Poorly
- Action Items (owner, due date, status columns)
- Lessons Learned

Format this as a reusable template page (not a live incident doc) so it can be duplicated for each new incident. Include placeholder text or bracketed prompts in each section to guide future authors.

Do not publish, share, or apply the template to any live workspace yet — this requires explicit approval before changes are applied. Once the draft page is prepared, present me with: the full draft content, its intended location in {{vendor}}, and a short checklist confirming all required sections are present. Then stop for human sign-off before creating or finalizing anything in the live workspace.
